changes.after: Build a runnable program from your Go code.

before: An executable program uses package main and a main function. Imports name packages whose exported operations the code uses, such as fmt.Println.

go build translates the program into an executable. The hands-on command below uses that build workflow. go run also builds before running, but is only a comparison here; lesson 41 gives its concrete module invocation. It is not an interpreter reading source statement by statement.
Editing main.go does not change an executable already built from an earlier version.
This course uses official Go 1.27.3. In the shared environment /usr/bin/go is an unrelated game, so validation uses the approved workspace-local compiler path.
Expected output or behavior: Ready. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: In a new folder save main.go. Use the installed Go toolchain to run go build -o lesson main.go, then ./lesson. Compare an edited source before and after rebuilding. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: `package main` and `func main()` give this program its starting point. The fmt package supplies the tool that displays a line.
A compiler turns code into a file the computer can run. `go build` does this work. `go run` builds the code and then runs it.
Changing the code does not change a file you already built. Build again to include your changes.
These examples use Go 1.27. The browser lets you read and explore them. Running them on your computer is optional and needs the Go tools installed.
The program shows `Ready` when it runs.

To try it, save the example as main.go in a new folder. Open a terminal, where you type commands. Run `go build -o lesson.exe main.go`, then run the new file. In Windows PowerShell use `.\lesson.exe`; on macOS or Linux use `./lesson.exe`. After editing the message, build again to update the file.

before.question: You edit main.go but run the previously built executable without rebuilding. What can appear?
choices: The old message from the previous build.
The executable downloads a new compiler automatically.
before.explanation: The earlier executable contains the old compilation, not the edited file.

after.question: You edit main.go, then run the old built file without rebuilding. What can appear?
after.explanation: The built file still contains the old instructions. Editing main.go alone does not update it.
